sentence: Levothyroxine is a medicine for an underactive thyroid, which is called hypothyroidism.
note: NHS page title: a medicine for an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).

sentence: The NHS says it suits most adults and children, though it is not right for everyone, so a clinician checks first.
note: Search summary of NHS page: suitable for most adults and children but not everyone; always check before taking.

sentence: It is also used after treatment for thyroid cancer, and some people take it after thyroid surgery.
note: Search results listed NHS trust leaflets on levothyroxine after total thyroid surgery and after thyroid cancer treatment; page titles only, MedlinePlus lists uses.

sentence: MedlinePlus, a US source, warns that it should not be used to lose weight, and that large amounts, especially with amphetamines, can cause serious or life-threatening harm.
note: MedlinePlus important warning, as quoted in search summary: large doses especially with amphetamines can be dangerous.

sentence: Levothyroxine is a man-made version of thyroxine, the main hormone the thyroid makes, so it stands in for what an underactive gland is not producing.
note: Existing page records NHS wording on synthetic T4; NHS treatment page describes levothyroxine replacing the missing hormone.

sentence: The NHS says treatment usually carries on for the rest of a person's life.
note: Search summary: NHS says treatment usually needs to continue for the rest of your life.

sentence: MedlinePlus says people are told to keep taking it even when they feel well, and not to stop without talking to their doctor.
note: MedlinePlus: continue levothyroxine even if you feel well; do not stop without talking to your doctor.

sentence: At first there are regular blood tests until the right amount is reached, which can take a while to get right.
note: Search summary: initially regular blood tests until correct dose reached.

sentence: Once the result is steady, the NHS says a blood test about once a year is usual.
note: Search summary: once stable, usually a blood test once a year.

sentence: Taking too much or too little can itself cause symptoms such as tiredness and weight changes, so a change in weight can be a sign that the dose needs reviewing.
note: Search summary of Leeds guidance: too much or too little can cause tiredness and weight gain; significant weight change may mean dose change. Attribution to Leeds page only loosely carried.

sentence: The NHS lists difficulty sleeping, headaches, feeling anxious, sweating and hair loss as the common side effects.
note: NHS common side effects as returned.

sentence: It says most side effects happen when the amount taken does not suit the person, and being on the wrong amount can cause feeling or being sick, diarrhoea, headaches or sleep problems.
note: Search summary: most side effects usually happen when dose is too high; wrong dose can cause sickness, diarrhoea, headaches, sleep problems.

sentence: Serious side effects are rare.
note: Search summary: serious side effects are rare.

sentence: A sudden rise in thyroid hormone, called thyroid crisis, can cause fever, a fast or irregular heartbeat, dizziness or fainting, and yellowing of the skin or eyes, and the NHS advises calling NHS 111 for suspected serious side effects.
note: Search summary: NHS lists thyroid crisis symptoms; advice for suspected serious side effects is to call NHS 111.

sentence: Signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as a swollen throat or tongue, a raised itchy rash or trouble breathing, need a 999 call.
note: NHS lists anaphylaxis symptoms; Sheffield Children's leaflet routes itchy rash or shortness of breath to 999. The NHS page's own routing wording was not visible in the excerpt.

sentence: Absorption is the weak point, and food, calcium and iron supplements, and antacids can reduce how much of the medicine the body takes up.
note: NHS lists interactions with calcium and iron supplements; Torbay leaflet says iron, calcium and some antibiotics interfere with absorption.

sentence: NHS trust leaflets say the tablet is taken on an empty stomach, apart from vitamin and mineral supplements, and before caffeinated drinks such as tea or coffee.
note: Search summaries of NHS trust leaflets: empty stomach, separate from supplements, before caffeine.

sentence: The NHS page also lists antidepressants such as sertraline among medicines that can interact.
note: Search summary: NHS page lists interactions with antidepressants such as sertraline and with calcium and iron supplements.

sentence: A pharmacist or doctor is the person to ask about any new medicine or herbal supplement.
note: NHS page has taking with other medicines section; advice to check with pharmacist or doctor is the NHS's usual framing, not directly quoted in results.

sentence: The NHS says levothyroxine can be taken in pregnancy if needed.
note: Search summary: NHS says it can be taken during pregnancy if needed.

sentence: Extra blood tests may be needed to check thyroid hormone levels and that the amount suits the person.
note: NHS: may need more blood tests in pregnancy.

sentence: UK hospital leaflets note that the amount often has to be raised early in pregnancy, and that most women return to their earlier amount after the birth.
note: Search summary of UK hospital guidance: dose needs increasing early in pregnancy; after birth most resume pre-pregnancy dose.

sentence: The NHS says levothyroxine can usually be taken while breastfeeding, but advises checking with a pharmacist or doctor first.
note: Search summary: usually can take while breastfeeding but check with pharmacist or doctor first.

sentence: Other NHS trust material says only small amounts reach breast milk, not enough to affect a baby's thyroid function.
note: Search summary: excreted into breast milk but not at levels sufficient to affect neonatal thyroid function; source page uncertain among the pregnancy hits.

sentence: The NHS says treatment for an underactive thyroid usually carries on for the rest of a person's life.
note: NHS: usually lifelong.

sentence: Blood tests are used at first to find the right amount, and once the result is steady a yearly check is usual.
note: Search summary.

sentence: MedlinePlus says people are told to keep taking it when they feel well and not to stop without speaking to their doctor.
note: MedlinePlus.

sentence: Levothyroxine treats the weight gain linked to an underactive thyroid, but taking too much or too little can itself cause weight changes and tiredness.
note: Leeds summary.

sentence: MedlinePlus warns against using it to lose weight when the thyroid works normally.
note: MedlinePlus warning.

sentence: A noticeable change in weight is a reason to talk to the GP, whose usual route is a routine GP appointment.
note: Not directly returned; framing of route to care. Marked as editorial routing.

sentence: A North and East Devon formulary page notes that levothyroxine stays in the body for a long time, so a missed tablet may be taken the next day.
note: Search summary of formulary: long half-life means missed dose may be taken next day.

sentence: Taking two doses together to make up for a missed one is generally not advised.
note: Search summary: don't take two doses together.

sentence: The Sheffield Children's leaflet says an extra tablet taken by mistake is unlikely to cause harm.
note: Search summary.

sentence: For taking too much, the NHS says to speak to a pharmacist, or call NHS 111 if none can be reached.
note: Search summary.
